primitives.name: DMCA Notice Density
primitives.verbatim_quote: # THE MOST ILLEGAL REPO ON GITHUB — RESEARCH VERDICT (2026-10-11) **Method**: cloned and mined `github/dmca` (the complete federal-style ledger of every DMCA takedown ever filed: **22,148 notices, 2013 → 2026-10**), live GitHub API state on 50+ flagship repos, HTTP 451 census, litigation history cross-check.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N_{\\text{DMCA}}': 'dimensionless count of notices', 'T': 'time interval [2013, 2026-10]', 'P_{\\text{class}}': 'probability of class being struck'}
primitives.assumptions: Notice count is Poisson-distributed over time; legal classes are independent.

layer2.mapping: Each repo maps to a probability distribution over legal risk; DMCA density = N_{\text{DMCA}} / (T × P_{\text{class}})
layer2.telemetry: Number of DMCA notices per repo-class

primitives.name: Illegal Class Frequency
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Most-struck project classes**: activation tools **369**, Vanced **260**, youtube-dl 68, yuzu 36, Ryujinx 20, Dolphin 18, Skyline 17, Popcorn 13, Lockpick 10, LibGen 7, Anna's Archive 5.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{\\text{class}}': 'frequency of class in notices', 'C_{\\text{class}}': 'count of repos in class'}
primitives.assumptions: Class frequency is proportional to legal enforcement intensity.

layer2.mapping: Frequency kernel F_{\text{class}} = N_{\text{DMCA}} / C_{\text{class}}; high values indicate strong legal targeting
layer2.telemetry: Repo-class notice counts normalized by class size

primitives.name: Legal Flag State
primitives.verbatim_quote: Today: `yuzu-emu/yuzu` = **404**; successor `suyu-emu/suyu` = **HTTP 451 "Unavailable For Legal Reasons"** — GitHub's own legal-removal flag; `shchmue/Lockpick_RCM` = **451** (Nintendo struck it 6+ times: 2023-05 ×4, 2024-02 ×2, 2024-03, 2024-09).
primitives.assumptions: Flagging is deterministic given prior strikes; state transitions are irreversible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: S_{\text{flag}} = 451 ⇒ repo is under legal embargo

layer2.mapping: Repo state S_{\text{flag}} maps to legal risk; 451 = legal shutdown signal
layer2.telemetry: HTTP status codes from GitHub API

The core insight is that GitHub’s legal ecosystem can be modeled as a stochastic dynamical system where repositories evolve through states of legality. The DMCA notice density (N_{\text{DMCA}}) acts as a proxy for legal risk, with higher values indicating stronger enforcement signals. The illegal class frequency (F_{\text{class}}) reveals which software categories are most targeted, such as activation tools (369 notices), suggesting a strong correlation between class legality and enforcement. The legal flag state (S_{\text{flag}}) provides a binary classification of repos into active, 451-flagged, or deleted states, reflecting the outcome of legal action. These three primitives form a triadic structure: legal risk = f(N_{\text{DMCA}}, F_{\text{class}}), and legal outcome = g(S_{\text{flag}}). The system exhibits non-reversible dynamics due to deletion and flagging, creating a causal arrow from enforcement to repo state. The failure mode occurs when enforcement is misapplied or absent, e.g., Microsoft never strikes massgravel/Microsoft-Activation-Scripts despite 369 notices, indicating a gap in legal enforcement or policy.
